failure_summary: Run 1 fails A7b: it never names the better column, saying only "the move that kept your threat ... alive" — the better-col/col3 alias IS offered in render_decision.zones.aliases but is absent from requiredSet (which lists only you-immediate c5r2, opp-key-square c3r4, you-immediate-line windows:c6r1,c5r2,c4r3,c3r4), so nothing obliged the model to name column 3; board-truth is otherwise sound (visualize_board on 3345533332552622 shows Gray major threats at col5 row2 [GT] and col5 row3, score -13, and 33455333325526262 shows Green occupying c3r4 at ply 17).
notes: n_runs=2 for this run (run_index 0..1), so the v1 sub-sampling rule collapses to grading every axis on every run; no nulls recorded. A1/A2/A6/G7a/G7b copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_2026-08-06T16-04-29Z_served_mechanical.json keys eval-49|D|0 and eval-49|D|1 (all pass). A3/A4/A5/A7/G1/G7-judgment graded on servedExplanation per the v2 addendum: the guard humanized every raw cNrM to "column N, row M" in both runs, so no coordinate-notation charge applies. Board verification: decision 334553333255262 (next Gray, scr col3=13, col7=0 => win_to_draw confirmed); afterBest 3345533332552622 gives Gray the stacked figure_7 pair c5r2[GT]+c5r3 (scr -13 for Green); afterPlayed 3345533332552626 leaves only c5r3 (scr col3=0, draw); the diagonal c6r1(O)/c5r2(empty)/c4r3(O)/c3r4 is real. Prompt rebuilt via assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(fv)): the Decision block states "Better move: column 3 (lands at c3r4)" verbatim, so the run-1 omission is not information suppression. G5: prompt threat lists (decision "major at c5r3 (you)"; afterBest "immediate at c5r2 (you)", "major at c5r3 (you)") are both board-true against the visualizer. G6: link L1 + guardrail match the after-best board (Gray completes its own double threat); patternOnAfterBestBoard=null did not misroute. G7: annotationRepairs empty in both runs; every handle wraps a role-matching phrase (run 1 keeps term:immediate_threat and zone:you-immediate on adjacent, non-nested words). Secondary, non-charged: run 1 wrote raw squares c6r1/c4r3 in prose against the prompt rule "Never write a raw square"; they were auto-promoted and rejected by the guard (guardDiagnostics.failures P5strong:cell_not_allowed:c6r1 and :c4r3, strippedSpecs [c6r1,c4r3]) — both cells are board-true Gray discs, the served prose is unharmed, and strippedSpecs is not annotationRepairs, so this is not a G7c auto-fail. Both runs frame the better move as keeping an immediate threat "alive" where the render frame says it completes/creates one; read at the line level (2 Gray discs + 2 empties on the decision board) this is defensible, so no A3/A4 charge, but it is the weakest wording in both answers.

counterexamples.evidence: Run 1 served text: "You should have played the move that kept your threat to make four next move alive on column 5, row 2 ..." — the better column is never stated; the only "column 3" in the string is the cell c3r4 the opponent takes. The assembled prompt states "Better move: column 3 (lands at c3r4)" and offers [zone:better-col], so the information was present and highlightable; requiredSet contains only c5r2, c3r4 and windows:c6r1,c5r2,c4r3,c3r4. Run 0, from the identical render, did wrap [zone:better-col]column 3[/zone:better-col] — the difference is obligation, not information.
